Topic: Valuation on the tilt (filling the Perfection.lean TODO)

Hi all — I'm Swami, currently a program manager at Google with a Ph.D. in Math from Texas A&M. I am working on a Lean formalization in the perfectoid/Fargues–Fontaine area outside of my Google work. I have a small RingTheory contribution I'd like to float before opening a PR, to check it's wanted and get a steer on one design point.

Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfection.lean carries a standing TODO, "Define the
valuation on the tilt." PreTilt.val exists and Tilt exists, but nothing
bridges them. I have a definition plus one @[simp] lemma that closes it, via
Valuation.extendToLocalization, with no new imports beyond
RingTheory/Valuation/ExtendToLocalization:

namespace Tilt

noncomputable def val : Valuation (Tilt K v O hv p) ℝ≥0 :=
  (PreTilt.val K v O hv p).extendToLocalization
    (S := nonZeroDivisors (PreTilt O p))
    (le_of_eq (PreTilt.supp_val ..).symm)   -- S ≤ v.supp.primeCompl
    (FractionRing (PreTilt O p))

@[simp] theorem val_algebraMap (x : PreTilt O p) :
    Tilt.val v hv p (algebraMap (PreTilt O p) (Tilt K v O hv p) x)
      = PreTilt.val K v O hv p x :=
  Valuation.extendToLocalization_apply_map_apply ..

end Tilt

The hypotheses are exactly PreTilt.val's own context — nothing extra, and it's fully general (no assumptions beyond the perfectoid-tilt setup already required for PreTilt.val).

One design question I'd like guidance on before opening the PR: Tilt is
currently a plain def, so algebraMap / IsLocalization don't resolve against it directly; my proof routes through FractionRing (PreTilt O p) and return-type defeq to sidestep that. Would you prefer Tilt be made reducible, or the relevant instances added, rather than the defeq route? Happy to shape the PR either way.

Does this look like something you'd take, and if so, any preference on the Tilt handling above?

@Swami Sethuraman Regarding

Would you prefer Tilt be made reducible, or the relevant instances added, rather than the defeq route?

which instances are you thinking of?

Thanks @Johan Commelin ! I dug into exactly what the defeq route is standing in for, and confirmed the fix end-to-end. Two instances, both one-line inferInstanceAs forwarders (since Tilt := FractionRing (PreTilt O p)):

noncomputable instance : Algebra (PreTilt O p) (Tilt K v O hv p) :=
  inferInstanceAs (Algebra (PreTilt O p) (FractionRing (PreTilt O p)))

instance : IsLocalization (nonZeroDivisors (PreTilt O p)) (Tilt K v O hv p) :=
  inferInstanceAs (IsLocalization (nonZeroDivisors (PreTilt O p)) (FractionRing (PreTilt O p)))

The second is IsFractionRing (PreTilt O p) (Tilt …) in idiomatic form. CommRing (Tilt …) already resolves via the field instance, so those two are the entire gap — extendToLocalization needs [Algebra A B] [IsLocalization S B], and against Tilt directly those two are what
#synth fails on (against FractionRing all three succeed).

With them in scope I've confirmed the whole Tilt.val definition and its characterizing lemma (extendToLocalization_apply_map_apply with B := Tilt) elaborate and build against Tilt directly — no FractionRing detour, no return-type defeq. So the instances fix it end-to-end, not just at the #synth level.

One placement note: the forwarders need [Fact (¬ IsUnit (p : O))] in scope (their RHS transitively needs CommRing (PreTilt O p), which lives under that Fact) — but that's exactly the section PreTilt.val and PreTilt's CommRing already sit in, so dropping them there adds no hypothesis beyond what the surrounding development already assumes.

The root cause is just that Tilt is a plain def, so instance search doesn't unfold it to see it's FractionRing (PreTilt O p). So there are two independent fixes: the two instances above (keeps Tilt opaque), or making Tilt reducible/abbrev (search unfolds it, no new instances needed). I'd lean toward the explicit instances — more robust if anyone later relies on Tilt being opaque — but you'll know better how Tilt's reducibility is used elsewhere, so I'm happy to shape the PR whichever way you'd prefer.

Thank you, Michael, for flagging the community guidelines and I duly note that. I did use AI to draft my post and my apologies, and I will avoid it going forward. Here is what I am proposing to address the first part of Perfection.lean TO DO: Defining valuation on the tilt.

Here is what we have so far in Mathlib:

1.      PreTilt has a valuation already – PreTilt.val

2.      Tilt is defined as the fraction field of the PreTilt. Tilt := FractionRing (PreTilt O p). Now Tilt doesn’t have a valuation yet.

3.      We want to extend the valuation from the PreTilt to the Tilt using the standard approach using Valuation.extendToLocalization.

4.      Now, Valuation.extendToLocalization needs the Algebra/IsLocalization instances to resolve against Tilt, and because Tilt is a plain def, search can't find them and my proposal is to accomplish this via forwarder instances or reducible with my recommendation being to use forwarder instances. I have checked that the forwarder route builds correctly against the current Tilt.
